pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/_shell/live.ts:1 The shell's store-reading modules are marked server-only, its one data action resolves the principal before it reads, and the browser half sends only the user's own Firebase ID token to the same-origin /api/session, so no store or vendor credential reaches the bundle.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/_shell/live.ts:1 The module is marked server-only (live.ts, headerFacts.ts), so the build refuses to put it in the client bundle. The technique's 'mark the module' rule is met.

app/(studio)/_shell/bellJobs.ts:22 The bell's server action authenticates the caller through the action core before it touches the kernel store with server privilege; the browser holds only its own session (session.ts:46 posts its idToken).
app/(studio)/_shell/headerFacts.ts:9 The store is reached only from a server-only module, so the browser never queries tables directly. Regime one does not hold.
app/(studio)/_shell/Providers.tsx:99 The shell's only fetches run in the browser against fixed same-origin paths. No server fetch takes an address that arrived as data.

app/(studio)/_shell/liveFeed.ts:61 The only value the client carries back is its own resume cursor. The client is the authority on its own position, and the cursor is not a server verdict that is trusted on return.

pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/floor/_floor/load.ts:1 The Floor reads every store in a server-only loader and hands the client island data plus port references, and an internal failure of the slot read reaches the browser through publicError as an opaque ref; no credential or raw internal fault crosses to the bundle.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/floor/_floor/load.ts:1 The loader that touches the kernel and v1 stores is marked server-only.
app/(studio)/floor/page.tsx:39 publicError keeps the classified codes and replaces an internal fault with an 'internal error (ref …)' envelope, logging the detail on the server.
app/(studio)/floor/_floor/load.ts:11 The SQLite store is opened server-side only, so the browser holds no store role.
app/(studio)/floor/_floor/load.ts:21 The browser never writes rows directly, so no row policy or defaulted owner column is in play.
app/(studio)/floor/_floor/Floor.tsx:119 The live feed is a browser-side EventSource to a fixed same-origin path. No server-side fetch takes a data-borne destination.
app/(studio)/floor/page.tsx:34 Round-tripped state is the person's own lane, month and slot address, parsed as input. No server verdict is carried back.

pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:49 The commit does not trust the preview token the browser carries back: it re-derives the v1 digest from a fresh read and the kernel recomputes the token, refusing a stale or forged one; every Board door authenticates its caller before it touches the server-privileged store.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:49 This is the technique's 're-derive it' branch. The client's token is compared against a server recomputation (real.ts:245 hands the token and a fresh v1Digest to kernelCommit), so a client cannot manufacture a pass.

app/(studio)/board/[packet]/keepalive/route.ts:24 The same-origin route guards the caller, caps the body and passes the input through a zod schema before it reaches the store. The server actions use principal('read') in the same way (actions.ts:33).
app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:1 The real port, the fixture port and load.ts are all marked server-only.
app/(studio)/board/_board/load.ts:43 Load and rail failures go through publicError (load.ts:49 for the rail), so an internal fault becomes a ref and the detail stays in the server log.
app/(studio)/board/_board/load.ts:32 The kernel store is opened on the server only, so the browser holds no store role.
app/(studio)/board/_board/Board.tsx:44 This is the browser's own keepalive to a same-origin path built from boardFor(id). No server fetch takes a data-borne address.

pairs.registryProposal: server-sealed-client-roundtrip could name the shape found here as a recognised realisation: a client-carried preview token is checked by comparing it against a server-side recomputation over freshly read state (optimistic concurrency), rather than by sealing. Today only the 're-derive it' exclusion covers it, in one sentence.
